open_points.subject: 50_public_apis_0_conventions.md:Conventions every operation follows — error path representation
open_points.text: with its kind and the path that names it — a field by its name and the names and list positions of the inputs that hold it, such as the alias of the second pick, a record by its kind and its id or position.
open_points.question: What exact public representation and segment order must an error path use?
options: A tagged array of name and numeric-position segments
open_points.default_guess: Use a tagged array of outermost-to-innermost segments.

witness.initial: An uploaded import file is kept, and the owner requests a mapping with a 41-character alias for the second pick.
events: The owner submits the picks and aliases.
migration_import reports the out-of-form alias in the mapping.
witness.observer: The owner-interface adapter or any semantic test comparing the mapping answer

open_points.subject: 50_public_apis_0_conventions.md:Conventions every operation follows — list-position numbering
open_points.text: a field by its name and the names and list positions of the inputs that hold it, such as the alias of the second pick
open_points.question: Are numeric list positions in paths zero-based or one-based?
options: Zero-based positions, so the second pick is 1
One-based positions, so the second pick is 2

witness.initial: An uploaded import file is kept, and only the alias supplied for the second pick is longer than 40 characters.
events: The owner asks for the import mapping.
witness.observer: The owner interface and clients that associate the failure with a submitted pick

open_points.subject: 50_public_apis_0_conventions.md:Conventions every operation follows — composite field failures
open_points.text: one entry for each failing field of the request, or each failing record or identity it names
open_points.question: When one validation rule concerns several fields together, does it produce one entry for the composite rule or one entry for every participating field?
options: One entry for the composite failure, attached to one defined path
One entry for each participating field
One entry at a defined request or object root
open_points.default_guess: Return one entry for the composite rule at a defined object-root path.

witness.initial: An active project is granted to a registered agent session and has no published estimate pointer.
events: Kernel calls publish with a valid request id and type but supplies neither uri nor payload_ref.
The stage-(4) check applies the rule that at least one reference must be present.
outcomes: One failure entry reports that the reference is missing.
Two failure entries report uri and payload_ref separately.
witness.observer: Kernel and the agent flow receiving the refusal

open_points.subject: 50_public_apis_0_conventions.md:Conventions every operation follows — record path selector
open_points.text: a record by its kind and its id or position.
open_points.question: When a failing record has both an id and a position, which one must its path use?
options: Always use the id when readable and use the position only when no id is readable
Carry both the id and the position
open_points.default_guess: Use the id when readable and fall back to the position only when it is not.

witness.initial: A picked project contains two malformed pointer records: the pointer at position 0 has id ffffffff-ffff-ffff-ffff-ffffffffffff, the pointer at position 1 has id 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000, and both have the same malformed-record error kind.
events: The owner asks for the import mapping.
The convention orders entries of that kind by path.
outcomes: Position-based paths put position 0 before position 1, reversing the two records' order.
witness.observer: The owner reading the mapping and tests comparing its ordered failures

open_points.subject: 50_public_apis_0_conventions.md:Conventions every operation follows — repeated identity occurrences
open_points.text: one entry for each failing field of the request, or each failing record or identity it names
open_points.question: If the same identity occurs more than once and that repetition is the failure, is there one entry for the identity or one entry for each offending occurrence?
options: One entry keyed by the repeated identity
One entry for every occurrence after the first
One entry for every occurrence including the first
open_points.default_guess: Return one entry for every occurrence after the first, with its occurrence path.

witness.initial: The kept import file contains project P, and no migration closure exists.
events: The owner requests a mapping whose picks name P twice.
A04 rule 6 refuses a pick given twice.
outcomes: The refusal contains one duplicate-pick entry naming P.
The refusal contains two entries, one for each path at which P was picked.
witness.observer: The owner interface displaying which submitted picks must be corrected

open_points.subject: 50_public_apis_0_conventions.md:Conventions every operation follows — deadline coincident with return
open_points.text: a call due while the previous call of the same pass is still running is not made, and the pass waits for the next due one; deadlines that pass during a suspension of the host or a long call are not made up. Each time a call returns, the pass takes one reading and waits for the first deadline at or after it
open_points.question: If a call returns exactly at the next fixed deadline, is that deadline treated as missed while the call was running or made immediately because it equals the post-return reading?
options: Skip that deadline and wait for the following one
Make the next call immediately at the equal deadline
open_points.default_guess: Make the call immediately, treating the return as complete before the equal post-return reading.

witness.initial: Serving began at monotonic reading 0, the first call starts at one interval, and it returns exactly at reading two intervals.
events: The second deadline and the first call's return coincide.
The pass takes its required post-return reading, which is exactly the second deadline.
outcomes: The second call is skipped and the next call occurs at the third deadline.
The second call is made immediately at the second deadline.
witness.observer: The module invoked by the pass and tests recording invocation times

open_points.subject: 50_public_apis_0_conventions.md:Conventions every operation follows — failed pass call
open_points.text: Each time a call returns, the pass takes one reading and waits for the first deadline at or after it; when its wait ends — on time, or late after a suspension — it makes one call, whatever deadlines its wait passed, and takes its next reading when that call returns.
open_points.question: Does a call that fails or raises count as returning for scheduling purposes, and does the pass continue or terminate?
options: Treat every completed attempt, including failure, as a return and continue scheduling
Terminate the pass after a failed call
Retry or reschedule failures under a separate rule
open_points.default_guess: Treat a failed completed attempt as a return, report the failure as applicable, and continue from one new reading.

witness.initial: The session-expiry pass is running normally and its next owner_sessions call encounters a runtime failure before producing an answer.
events: The call fails instead of returning normally.
Another interval elapses while the process remains up.
outcomes: The pass takes a new reading after the failure and invokes owner_sessions again at a later deadline.
The pass has terminated and makes no later invocation.
witness.observer: The owner whose expired sessions are or are not removed, and the host observing pass activity
